backlog.title: Make the state lock's warn-and-proceed path crash-safe on Windows rename contention
backlog.detail: Observed 2026-08-07 in a full-suite run: two workers hit the 5000ms lock timeout, both proceeded unlocked, and their concurrent state.json renames collided — EPERM from fs.renameSync crashed the worker (tests/state.test.mjs 'concurrent state updates are serialized by the state lock'). The warn-and-proceed escape hatch exists for availability, so its unlocked write must tolerate rename contention (bounded retry with jitter on EPERM/EACCES, then a loud failure) instead of throwing on first collision. Chassis change: state.mjs in BOTH plugins (literal-swap mirror via npm run sync-chassis); extend the contention test to pin the no-crash contract on the escape-hatch path.

disposition.notes: Bounded rename-contention retry in the atomic write; Codex analysis delegated (first run likely-dead, cancelled; refined re-delegation returned approve-with-corrections, applied)
